proposal: The Mandate recommends legislation to repeal the federal sugar program and, ideally, the ARC and PLC programs, to stop duplicate ARC/PLC and crop insurance payments in the same year, and to cap the taxpayer share of crop insurance premiums at 50 percent or less. It also urges USDA to refrain from using the Commodity Credit Corporation's discretionary spending authority and Congress to repeal or narrow it.
remaining: Repeal of the federal sugar program (the program was instead extended through crop year 2031).
Repeal of ARC and PLC (the programs were instead reauthorized through 2031 with higher support levels).
A ban on receiving ARC/PLC payments and a crop insurance indemnity in the same year (no such provision in the sources reviewed).
A cap of 50 percent or less on the taxpayer share of crop insurance premiums (the 2025 law instead raised several subsidies, and current rate tables list rates above 50 percent).
Repeal or narrowing of CCC section 5 discretionary authority, and USDA refraining from using it.

status_summary: Policy has moved in the opposite direction on the main points. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) raised ARC/PLC reference prices for crop years 2025 through 2030, raised the ARC guarantee from 86 to 90 percent of benchmark revenue, authorized up to 30 million new base acres, raised the payment limit to $155,000, and extended the sugar program through crop year 2031 with higher loan rates; USDA's rule estimates a 10-year ARC/PLC cost increase of about $46 billion. USDA also established an $11 billion Farmer Bridge Assistance program under section 5(b) of the CCC Charter Act (final rule 2026-02-23), the type of discretionary authority the Mandate advised against using. The House-passed 2026 farm bill makes no change to ARC/PLC covered commodities, and USDA's Risk Management Agency bulletin of 2025-08-20 shows crop insurance subsidies raised for the Supplemental Coverage Option and for beginning farmers, with no 50 percent premium cap shown. The Senate Agriculture Committee advanced its farm bill 12 to 11 on 2026-09-16, and the latest extension of the 2018 farm bill ended on 2026-09-30 with no new long-term farm bill enacted.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed (GovInfo dates it 2025-07-04). Its agriculture provisions (title I, subtitle C) raise ARC/PLC reference prices (section 10301), add up to 30 million base acres (section 10302) and raise the payment limit from $125,000 to $155,000 (section 10307); USDA implemented them in the 2026-01-12 rule below. Its sugar provisions (section 10312) are covered in the 2026-07-09 entry.

USDA's Risk Management Agency issues Manager's Bulletin MGR-25-006 implementing crop insurance changes from Public Law 119-21: the Supplemental Coverage Option subsidy rate rises from 65 to 80 percent (same increase for ECO and similar options), beginning farmers and ranchers receive added premium subsidy, and Whole-Farm Revenue Protection maximum coverage rises from 85 to 90 percent. The bulletin's rate table lists premium subsidies above 50 percent at several coverage levels (for example 67 percent at the 50 percent level for basic and optional units).

FSA and CCC publish the rule implementing the law's ARC, PLC and Dairy Margin Coverage changes: ARC guarantee 90 percent, ARC payment cap 12 percent of benchmark revenue, payment limit $155,000, up to 30 million new base acres; estimated 10-year ARC/PLC cost increase of $46.2 billion.

CCC final rule creates the Farmer Bridge Assistance program, about $11 billion in one-time payments to 2025-crop producers, using section 5(b) of the CCC Charter Act; USDA describes it as a bridge until higher reference-price payments arrive after October 1, 2026.

The House passes H.R. 7567 (224 to 200). Per CRS, it makes no change to the commodities eligible for ARC, PLC or marketing assistance loans, directs the President to prioritize domestic sugar production for domestic food use, and raises premium subsidies for veteran farmers.

The Senate Agriculture chairman releases a discussion draft (Agriculture Act of 2026) that, per CRS, clarifies sugar loan provisions and calls for a study on adding dry edible beans to covered commodities.
CCC final rule implements the law's sugar provisions: program extended from crop year 2025 through 2031 and loan rates raised.

The Senate Agriculture Committee advances its 2026 farm bill 12 to 11 on a party-line vote after resuming a recessed business meeting; the report quotes an industry analyst saying a Senate floor vote is unlikely before the pre-midterm recess.

title: Cut farm subsidies (sugar, ARC/PLC, crop insurance) and curb CCC discretionary aid
uncertainties: Crop insurance: the Risk Management Agency bulletin (MGR-25-006, 2025-08-20) was read and shows the law raised the Supplemental Coverage Option subsidy and beginning farmer subsidy and lists general subsidy rates above 50 percent; the bulletin does not give prior rates, so whether the general rates themselves changed is not shown, and the statute text of the crop insurance sections was not read. The actual new sugar loan rates were not read. Farm bill reporting after 2026-07-29 comes from the University of Illinois Farm Policy News site (secondary); the Senate committee bill text was not read, and the Farm Policy News report does not describe its ARC, PLC, sugar or crop insurance provisions, so those are unassessed. A separate specialty crop assistance rule (published 2026-06-01) and the December 2025 announcement of the bridge program were not reviewed. Whether section 5(b) is the exact subsection the Mandate meant by its section 5 discretionary authority is an interpretation.
